newsitem.title: POLAND: Probe of Polish priest's remarks on Jews dropped.
newsitem.headline: Probe of Polish priest's remarks on Jews dropped.

text.p: Polish prosecutors on Wednesday dropped legal proceedings against prominent Catholic priest Henryk Jankowski for allegedly anti-Semitic remarks made during a sermon in 1995, their spokeswoman said.
"The prosecutor discontinued proceedings because the degree of social harm caused by (the priest's) action was not substantial," Gdansk prosecutors' office spokeswoman Maria Jezowska-Kamirska said.
She told Reuters the proceedings could be reopened if Jankowski, once a close associate of former Solidarity union chief Lech Walesa, offended again.
In the sermon Jankowski, who heads a parish in the northern city of Gdansk, allegedly compared the star of David with the communist hammer and sickle and the Nazi swastika.
The sermon was attended by the then Polish President Walesa, who lost a race for his second term later in 1995 to ex-commmunist Aleksander Kwasniewski.
Walesa was at the time reproached for failing to instantly condemn Jankowski's words, which he said he had not heard. He later issued a statement strongly condemning anti-Semitism.
The Catholic Church distanced itself from the priest's words.

Jankowski, a prominent supporter of the Solidarity union in its pre-1989 fight against communist rule, also allegedly said the Polish people should not allow those who owed secret allegiance to Israel or Russia to remain in government.
He might have faced up to three years in prison if the prosecutor had decided to press charges in court.

Most of Poland's 3.5 million Jews were murdered by Nazi occupation forces during World War Two. Thousands of survivors left in subsequent waves of emigration, notably during an anti-Jewish campaign mounted by a nationalist faction of the ruling Communist Party in 1968.
